clue.text: Many draw behind on scorn being shown

indicators.note: behind places the word for draw after the letters for many and on

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
to draw someone in is to tempt or lure them

explanation.surface: A crowd cheers on the losing side while derision is openly displayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' puts TEMPT after C and ON; 'being shown' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt and scorn are synonyms, both meaning disdain for something thought worthless.

clue.text: Despicable guy the underworld finds a worm

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm

explanation.surface: A villain goes down to hell and comes across a creeping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddis worm is the larva of the caddis fly, which anglers use as bait.

clue.text: Things may appear quite different after dark

indicators.note: the word Things takes on another look, its letters rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Familiar objects look strange once the light has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nights, used as an adverb, means at night, during the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Colours in green. Significant, that

indicators.note: in tells us the answer is tucked inside the run of words green Significant

explanation.surface: A remark that green is the shade on a flag carries special meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: The full stop is ignored: the letters run on from 'green' into 'Significant'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, and colours is the military word for a regiment's flag.

clue.text: Temporary home provided for a Frenchman-about time!

indicators.note: about means the French name goes around the word for time

parts.note: Pierre is a typical French man's name
a date is a time fixed for something

explanation.surface: Lodgings are arranged for a visitor from France, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided for' is link wording. PIERRE is split as PIE...RRE around DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-a-terre is a small flat kept for occasional stays, a second base in town.

clue.text: Go round inflictinghurt

parts.note: a ring is a circle, something round

explanation.surface: Making a circuit while causing injury, like a bull in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue runs 'inflicting hurt' together as one word; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Goring is wounding with horns or tusks, a way of causing injury.

clue.text: Reading love poetry when abroad

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
verse is poetry
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone reads romantic poems while travelling in foreign parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' is link wording here, though it tempts as the English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas means in a foreign country, across the sea: a synonym for abroad.

clue.text: Bad spirit permissible — it's taken for granted

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous demon
licit means lawful or allowed

explanation.surface: A mischievous sprite is allowed, and nobody questions it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is understood without being stated, assumed rather than spelt out.

clue.text: Agents in error ordering flowers

indicators.note: in error suggests the letters of Agents in have gone wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Spies make a mistake when ordering a bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' is the anagram signal; 'ordering' links fodder to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentians are blue-flowered mountain plants, so they are examples of flowers.

clue.text: Dealt with food compendium written by a leading journalist

indicators.note: written by puts the journalist's letters after the compendium, as a byline follows

parts.note: a digest is a summary or compilation of material
ED is short for editor, the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A food anthology penned by a top newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Digested means broke down a meal in the stomach, processing what was eaten.

clue.text: Frank has joined a military service to start all over

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
frank and open both mean candid

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank enlists in the army to begin a new life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has joined' is link wording: the RE simply comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To reopen is to open again or resume, begin a second time.

clue.text: Entire get-up of neat girl

indicators.note: a get-up is an outfit, so the letters of neat girl are dressed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A complete outfit belonging to a tidy young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral can mean whole or complete, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Like one's doubling back in Italy

parts.note: as means like, as in 'white as snow'

indicators.note: back means the doubled run is then read in reverse
doubling means the letters for one's appear twice over

parts.note: one's is read as one is, I plus IS, giving the letters IS

explanation.surface: Someone doubles back on themselves while touring Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubling' makes ISIS and 'back' turns it to SISI, after AS. The definition is cryptic: a place found in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Assisi is a hill town in Umbria, home of St Francis, so it lies within that country.

clue.text: Still having had no proposal?

definitions.meaning: still means not moving at all
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting, so being without one is read playfully

explanation.definitionFit: Motionless means stationary, unmoving; read as motion-less it also means lacking a formal proposal.

clue.text: Not ideal, so may result in ruin

indicators.note: may result in shows the letters of Not ideal so produce something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Falling short of the ideal can lead to disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolation means devastation, a state of waste and wreckage.

clue.text: Put together the jumble brought back in expert fashion

indicators.note: in places the reversed jumble inside the word for expert

parts.note: able means skilled or competent

indicators.note: brought back in a down clue means the jumble word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a mess is a jumble or muddle

explanation.surface: Someone tidies away a jumble sale's remains with practised skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns MESS into SSEM, which 'in' places inside ABLE. 'fashion' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to fit parts together or construct.

clue.text: Date once arranged, so the story goes

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of Date once are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a rendezvous was once set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so the' and 'goes' are link wording around the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short personal tale or account of an incident.

clue.text: Edges up to the top man, smiling foolishly

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for edges is read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: rims are edges or borders
the king is the man at the top of the realm

explanation.surface: A courtier sidles towards the monarch with a silly grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RIMS into SMIR; 'to' links it to KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Smirking is smiling in a smug or silly way.

clue.text: Flier presenting elegant appearance outside and in

indicators.note: outside means the stylish word wraps around the word and

parts.note: smart means stylish, and a smart look is an elegant appearance
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird with a dapper look both inside and out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps SMART round AND to give SANDMART, then IN follows. 'presenting' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand martin is a small brown swallow-like bird, so it is a flier.

clue.text: A woman quietly cooking a meal

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for soft playing

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of a meal are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A lady softly preparing dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Pamela is a female given name, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Clap eyes on an article and feel furious

parts.note: to clap eyes on is to see
the is the definite article in grammar

explanation.surface: Someone spots a newspaper piece that makes their blood boil.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly enraged, boiling with anger.

clue.text: Points to the heart again

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
the core is the heart or centre of something

explanation.surface: Someone gestures towards the centre of their chest once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Encore is called out by an audience wanting a repeat, meaning once more.

clue.text: Not yet 18, and modelling nude madness!

indicators.note: modelling shapes the letters of nude into a new form

parts.note: rage is fury, a kind of madness

explanation.surface: Outrage that a teenage girl has posed without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelling' turns NUDE into UNDE, then RAGE follows; 'and' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: Under age means below the legal age, which in Britain is eighteen for adulthood.

clue.text: Reserve that's essential for the betting man

parts.note: to book is to reserve a seat or table
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Booking ahead is vital for the gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookie, short for bookmaker, takes bets on races and other events.

clue.text: Deferential, yet sees the French dream slashed

parts.note: reve is French for a dream
rent, past tense of rend, means torn or slashed

explanation.surface: Respectful still, though a cherished hope is cut to ribbons.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means showing deep respect, as deferential people do.

clue.text: " is Eternal Delight. Blake" (The Voice of the Devil)

definitions.text: " is Eternal Delight. Blake" (The Voice of the Devil)

parts.words: " is Eternal Delight. Blake" (The Voice of the Devil)
parts.note: fill the blank in William Blake's line from The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, spoken by the Devil

clue.text: These days being in flight can be an exciting adventure

indicators.note: being in places the era letters inside the word for flight

parts.note: flight means running away, an escape
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: Nowadays air travel can be a thrilling experience.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or reckless exploit, a lively adventure.
